stories.title: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq rise after July jobs report misses badly
stories.summary: U.S. stocks climbed on Friday after the July jobs report came in well below expectations, with the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all advancing. Investors weighed the weak print against what it could mean for the Federal Reserve's next policy move.
stories.whyItMatters: A soft labor market print that still sends stocks higher signals investors are pricing in a more accommodative Fed, a dynamic worth tracking heading into the next rate decision.
whatToWatch: Any Fed commentary reacting to the jobs data
Whether the rally extends into next week's sessions
questions: Does this move reflect rate-cut optimism or something else driving the gains?

sources.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq rise after July jobs report surprises to the downside

stories.title: U.S. economy unexpectedly shed 23,000 jobs in July
stories.summary: The U.S. labor market unexpectedly contracted in July, losing 23,000 jobs, according to CNBC. The decline runs counter to expectations for continued job growth and marks a notable downside surprise in the government's monthly employment report.
stories.whyItMatters: Payrolls are a core input for the Fed's rate-decision calculus, and an outright job loss — rather than just slower growth — raises the stakes for how policymakers respond.
whatToWatch: Revisions to prior months' payroll figures
How the Fed characterizes the labor market in upcoming commentary
questions: Is this an isolated soft reading or the start of a broader slowdown?

sources.title: U.S. economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July

stories.title: NY Fed survey shows little change in inflation expectations for July
stories.summary: The New York Fed's latest survey found consumer inflation expectations were largely unchanged in July, according to Yahoo Finance. The steady reading comes as markets separately digest a weak July jobs report.
stories.whyItMatters: Stable inflation expectations give the Fed more room to focus on labor-market weakness without worrying inflation psychology is drifting, a key factor in how aggressively it might cut rates.
whatToWatch: Upcoming CPI and PCE inflation data
The Fed's next policy statement for how it balances jobs weakness against inflation
questions: Will expectations stay anchored if the labor market continues to soften?

stories.title: Space stocks surge: SpaceX-linked names, Intuitive Machines, Rocket Lab jump
stories.summary: Space-sector stocks rallied sharply, with Intuitive Machines up 9% and Rocket Lab up 8%, alongside an 11% move tied to SpaceX, as Wall Street turned more bullish on the group, per Yahoo Finance.
stories.whyItMatters: A broad, double-digit-percentage rally across multiple space names suggests a sector-wide sentiment shift rather than a single-company story, which matters for investors tracking momentum in speculative growth pockets.
whatToWatch: Whether gains hold or fade in subsequent sessions
Any analyst notes explaining the shift in sentiment
questions: What specifically changed Wall Street's view on space stocks this week?

stories.title: Doximity shares surge 50% on medical AI enthusiasm
stories.summary: Shares of Doximity skyrocketed 50% as investors grew excited about the company's medical AI positioning, according to MarketWatch. The move raises the question of whether such a sharp, fast rally can be sustained.
stories.whyItMatters: A 50% single-name pop is an outsized move that highlights how much investor appetite for AI-adjacent healthcare plays has grown, and outsized rallies often invite scrutiny of valuation.
whatToWatch: Follow-through trading in the days after the spike
Analyst reaction and any price-target changes
questions: Is the rally supported by a fundamental catalyst or largely sentiment-driven?

questions: What in the earnings report specifically drove the move?

stories.title: Viral 'back-to-school haul' trend pushes some parents to spend big
stories.summary: A MarketWatch report highlights one mother who spent $2,000 outfitting her kindergartner, as viral 'back-to-school haul' videos on TikTok and YouTube fuel escalating spending pressure among parents.
stories.whyItMatters: Back-to-school spending is a closely watched read on consumer discretionary strength, and social-media-driven spending trends can move sales at retailers who cater to families.
whatToWatch: Broader back-to-school retail sales data as the season progresses
questions: How representative is this spending level of the average back-to-school shopper?
